parties:
Karam Ali  ----- Appellant
Vs.
State ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saba J: This jail appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 30-4-95 passed by the 2nd Assistant Sessions Judge, Narayanganj in Sessions Case No. 7 of 1994 convicting accused Karam Ali under section 399 of the Penal Code and sentencing him thereunder to suffer RI for 7 years and to pay a fine of Taka 2,000 only, in default, to suffer RI for a further period of 6 months. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that on getting a secret information through a tip at about 9-30 PM on 23-5-93 to the effect that some miscreants were making preparation for committing dacoity, informant SI Md Abdul Halim Mia of Narayanganj PS entered the said fact in the GD and set out with a contingent of police force consisting of SI Md Maisar Ali Khan, constable Nikhil Chandra, constable Abdul Hamid, constable Mir Box, constable Helal, constable Abu Abdullah and constable Faruque Hossain for apprehending the miscreants. The informant and his accompanying police force at about 1-30 PM found 7/8 young men boarding an engine driven-boat in the Shitalakhya river and started moving towards a certain direction. The informant party followed them. When the said boat came near Sonakanda Ghat the informant party tried to stop the engine boat but the miscreants getting scent of the arrival of the police party moved on desperately and started towards Maula Ghat on the western bank of the Shitalakhya river, after throwing away the incriminating articles and weapons with them. The informant and his men hotly chased them. In the process informant SI Abdul Halim Meah and his companions arrested accused Karam Ali, who confessed his guilt and stated to the informant and his men that he along with 7/8 of his companions were preparing for committing dacoity at the Kumudini Jute Godown, Narayanganj. 

 4. Upon the aforesaid allegations accused Karam Ali and three others were put on trial before the 2nd Assistant Sessions Judge, Narayanganj, in Sessions Case No. 7 of 1994 to answer a charge under section 399 of the Penal Code. 

 5. At the trial, the prosecution examined 11 witnesses and exhibited some documents in support of its case while the defence examined none. 

 9. To arrive at a correct decision in the case, it will be appropriate for us to consider the material evidence on record. 

 10. PW 1 Kaisar Ali Khan ASI stated in his evidence that on the night following 25-3-93 he got a secret information of commission of a dacoity at Kumudini Jute Godown by using an engine boat, following which informant SI Abdul Halim and a contingent of police force started to apprehend the miscreants. They noticed an engine boat moving in the Shitalakhya river with a group of persons in it and they followed it by an engine boat. As the complainant party chased the miscreants, the miscreants reached Maula Ghat and started running away. After a little chase, the informant and his force caught hold of accused Karam Ali. On interrogation, accused Karam Ali disclosed that he and 7/8 of his companions had assembled for committing dacoity at the Kumudini Jute Godown. The accused also disclosed to the raid party the names of the three co-accused and others involved in the case. 

 11. In cross-examination he denied the defence suggestion that accused Karam Ali was not one of the miscreants who had assembled for committing dacoity. 

 12. PW 2 Faroque Hossain, a police constable, stated in his evidence that he was a member of the raid party under SI Md Abdul Hakim Miah, on the night following 23-5-93. He stated that on getting a secret information that some miscreants had assembled for committing dacoity, the police party proceeded towards the place of assembly. They saw 7/8 miscreants in an engine boat moving in the Shitalakhya river. Getting scent of the arrival of the police party, the miscreants got down at Maula Ghat and started running away. The police party charsed the miscreants and arrested accused Karam Ali while the other miscreants managed to escape. He identified accused Karam Ali in the dock. 

 19. PW 9 Nikhil Kumar Basu is the police constable who was a member of the raid party on the fateful night of 23-5-93. He stated in his evidence that on getting a secret information that some miscreants had assembled for committing dacoity, a contingent of police force under the SI Md Abdul Hakim Miah started for the place of assembly and found an engine boat, with some miscreants in it, moving in the river Shitalakhya. Getting scent of the arrival of the police party, the miscreants got down at Maula Ghat and started running away. The police party chased them and apprehended accused Karam Ali, who later disclosed to them that he and 7/8 of his companions had assembled for committing dacoity at the Kumudini Jute Godown. The defence could not get any material from him that may discredit his evidence. 

 22. In this case, the prosecution has failed to examine informant SI Md Abdul Halim in spite of exhausting all legal processes for securing his attendance in the Court. Informant SI Md Abdul Halim Miah is no longer in service and his attendance could not be secured in spite of best efforts made by prosecution. In this case, it is true that the local witnessed did not support the prosecution case, PW 1 ASI Kaisar Ali Khan, PW 2 constable Md Faroque Hossain and PW 9 constable Nikhil Kumar Basu are witnesses to the occurrence and they were members of the police contingent deputed to apprehend the miscreants, who had assembled to commit dacoity at the Kumudini Jute Godown at Narayanganj. All these witnesses uniformly and consistently supported the prosecution case without any major contradiction in their evidence. We do not find any reason to disbelieve their corroborative evidence. The learned Assistant Sessions Judge was fully justified in relying on their evidence. We have already found that investigation officer of the case could not be examined by the prosecution due to circumstances beyond the control of the prosecution. In the facts of the case, we do not find any reason to hold that the defence has been prejudiced for non-examination of the investigation officer, although non-examination of the investigation officer in a. criminal case is usually viewed with disapproval. 

 25. From a reading of section 391 of the Penal Code it is crystal clear that to constitute the offence of 'dacoity' there must be 5 or more persons taking part in the offence. In our case under review, the charge specifically stated that only 4 accused had assembled for committing dacoity and accused Karam Ali was one of them. In such view of the matter, we hold that the charge under section 399 of the Penal Code is neither proper nor legal. In the facts of the case, there could be a charge for preparation for committing robbery, for which no specific penal section has been prescribed. We also do not find any specific section in the Penal Code prescribing punishment for assembly of miscreants numbering upto four for committing robbery, although specific provisions for punishment for assembly and preparation for committing dacoity have been provided in sections 399 and 402 of the Penal Code. This important aspect of law has so far escaped the attention of all concerned. It appears to us as an accidental omission in the Penal Code, which deserves to be brought to the notice of the legislature. We would, therefore, recommend to the Government for taking necessary steps towards amendment of the Penal Code for incorporating new sections in the Penal Code providing punishment for preparation and assembly of persons not exceeding four for committing robbery as defined in section 394 of the Penal Code. 

 26. In the instant case there are sufficient materials on record to find that 8/9 miscreants assembled for committing dacoity at Kumudini Jute Godown at Narayanganj Although the charge as framed in the case under section 399 of the Penal Code appears to be patently defective, yet there are sufficient materials on record to justify the conviction of accused appellant Karam Ali under section 399 of the Penal Code, he being a member of the assembly consisting of 8/9 persons for committing dacoity. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, we are inclined to hold that the accused appellant has not at all been prejudiced by the defect in the charge. We are also satisfied that the learned Assistant Sessions Judge was justified in passing the impugned order of conviction and sentence against the accused appellant on assigning cogent reasons. We find no merit in the appeal. The appeal fails accordingly. 

 27. In the result, the appeal is dismissed and the impugned judgment and order dated 30-4-95 passed by the learned 2nd Assistant Sessions Judge, Narayanganj in Sessions Case No. 7 of 1994 convicting accused appellant Karam Ali under section 399 of the Penal Code and sentencing him thereunder to suffer RI for 7(seven) years and to pay a fine of Taka 2,000.00, in default, to suffer RI for a further period of 6 months are affirmed.
